admission.justification: Two tests pin the unchanged item rules and the single-item true conflict at the incoming number, so a future merge change that splits a true conflict or reorders precedence fails before it lands.

applicability: Sidecar, record and Markdown merges after alignment, in crossing and ordinary converted syncs.
conditions: A reference both lines changed differently stays one conflict item at the incoming number.
exclusions: Rule-7-skipped cards, where the legacy numbering-collision reason may still fire.

evidence: Rationale: after alignment the sidecar merges by number through the unchanged key/item machinery, so a reference both lines changed differently is still one conflict item at the incoming number, and authored/mechanical precedence is untouched. Observed: test_a_true_conflict_stays_one_item_at_the_incoming_number; both-added same-number integration now aligns to a fresh number (test_a_reference_number_both_lines_added_is_aligned_to_a_fresh_number) instead of the pre-R66 collision.

statement: Rule 5 existing merge: sidecars merge by aligned number and Markdown by line with unchanged authored/mechanical rules; true conflicts stay one item
